'''Ian Alexander Walmsley''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE|FRS}} (born 1960)<ref name="WhosWho">{{cite web |url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U42154/WALMSLEY_Prof._Ian_Alexander?index=9&results=QuicksearchResults&query=0 |title=Walmsley, Prof. Ian Alexander PhD; FRS 2012 |work=[[Who's Who]] |publisher=A & C Black |orig-date=2007-12-01|date=2024-12-01|access-date=2025-08-21}}</ref> is Provost of [[Imperial College London]] where he is also Chair of Experimental Physics. He was previously pro-vice-chancellor for research and Hooke Professor of Experimental Physics at the [[University of Oxford]],<ref name="WhosWho"/>  and a professorial fellow at [[St Hugh's College, Oxford]].<ref name='provc'>{{cite web | url = http://www.ox.ac.uk/media/news_stories/2009/090219_1.html | title = New Pro-Vice-Chancellor for Research | access-date = 2012-04-20 | date = 2009-02-19 | publisher = [[University of Oxford]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121202160901/http://www.ox.ac.uk/media/news_stories/2009/090219_1.html | archive-date = 2012-12-02 | url-status = dead }}</ref>  He is also director of the [[NQIT]] (Networked Quantum Information Technologies) hub within the UK National Quantum Technology Programme, which is led by the University of Oxford.<ref name="NQIT">{{cite web |url=http://nqit.ox.ac.uk/people/ian |title=Prof Ian Walmsley: NQIT Hub Director |work=Networked Quantum Information Technologies |publisher=[[University of Oxford]] |access-date=2016-01-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305000822/http://nqit.ox.ac.uk/people/ian |archive-date=2016-03-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is also a Fellow of the Institute of Physics, the American Physical Society and the Optical Society of America.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/about/leadership-and-strategy/provost/about-the-provost/ |access-date=8 March 2022|title=About the Provost }}</ref> He will return to Oxford from October 2025 as Director of the [[Oxford Quantum Institute]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Ian Walmsley to lead Oxford Quantum Institute |url=https://www.physics.ox.ac.uk/news/professor-ian-walmsley-lead-oxford-quantum-institute |website=Physics News |publisher=University of Oxford |access-date=12 May 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Manuschka |first1=Jacob |title=Professor Ian Walmsley to lead Oxford Quantum Institute |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/25168326.professor-ian-walmsley-lead-oxford-quantum-institute/ |access-date=19 May 2025 |work=[[Oxford Mail]] |date=17 May 2025}}</ref>

Walmsley was educated at [[Imperial College London]], and [[The Institute of Optics]], [[University of Rochester]].<ref name='provc'/> He received the [[Joseph F. Keithley Award|Joseph F. Keithley Award For Advances in Measurement Science]] in 2011<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/199711/keithley.cfm |title= APS Joseph F. Keithley Award: Presentation of check to endow the APS Joseph F. Keithley Award for Advances in Measurement Science |author=<!--Not stated--> |publisher= American Physical Society |access-date= 16 May 2018 }}</ref> and was elected a fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 2012<ref name='FRS'>{{cite web | url = http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/new-fellows-2012/ | title = New Fellows 2012 | access-date = 2012-04-20 | date = 2012-04-19 | publisher = [[Royal Society]]}}</ref> for his contributions to [[quantum optics]] and [[Ultrashort pulse|ultrafast optics]],<ref name='RSbio'>{{cite web | url = https://royalsociety.org/people/ian-walmsley-12481/ | title = Professor Ian Alexander Walmsley FRS | access-date = 2016-03-30 | publisher = [[Royal Society]]}}</ref> including his development of the [[spectral phase interferometry for direct electric-field reconstruction]] (SPIDER) technique.

In March 2018 it was announced that Walmsley had been appointed [[Provost of Imperial College London|provost]] of [[Imperial College London]], succeeding [[James Stirling (physicist)|James Stirling]] on 1 September 2018.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/185070/oxford-provice-chancellor-eminent-physicist-appointed/|title=Oxford Pro-Vice-Chancellor and eminent physicist appointed as new Provost {{!}} Imperial News {{!}} Imperial College London|work=Imperial News|access-date=2018-03-02|language=en-GB}}</ref>

In October 2019, Walmsley co-founded [[Orca Computing]], to undertake [[Quantum Computing]] in [[Optical Fibre]] through the use of [[quantum memory]].
